patches.why: Remove the public CDN address of the Python runtime (a third-party host).

patches.old:
if (!prefs.use_online_access) {
    const msg = 'Python needs to download its runtime, but online access is turned off (Preferences ▸ System ▸ Network).';
patches.new:
if (prefs.use_online_access || !prefs.use_online_access) {
    const msg = 'Python is not available on Homestead: its runtime would be downloaded from a public web server. JavaScript scripting works without it.';
patches.why: Python is refused with a plain message instead of downloading a runtime from a third-party host.

patches.new: load: () => Promise.reject(new Error('Python is not available on Homestead')) as Promise<PyodideModule>,
patches.why: No dynamic import of a runtime from a public address.
Name no third-party host in the unreachable download message.

patches.old: | Pyodide | 314.0.7 | MPL-2.0 (CPython: PSF License) | cdn.jsdelivr.net/pyodide/v314.0.7/full/ | Python scripting. Downloaded unmodified from the CDN the first time Python is used; JavaScript scripting works offline without it. |
patches.new: | Pyodide | 314.0.7 | MPL-2.0 (CPython: PSF License) | not shipped | Python scripting. Not available on Homestead (the runtime would be downloaded from a public web server); JavaScript scripting works offline without it. |
patches.why: The licence notice names the public CDN; Python is off on Homestead.

patches.old: const sloppyEval = new Function('__scope', '__src', 'with (__scope) { return eval(__src); }') as (scope: object, src: string) => unknown;
patches.why: The console built a code evaluator when the module loaded; under the appliance policy (no unsafe-eval, ADR-057) that stopped the whole app from starting. The console now answers with a message instead.

patches.old: return { ok: false, error: `SyntaxError: ${msg}`, line: syntaxErrorLine(code, msg) };
patches.new: return { ok: false, error: `${msg.includes('eval') ? "Scripts and the console cannot run on Homestead: the page's security policy does not allow running code typed into the app." : `SyntaxError: ${msg}`}`, line: msg.includes('eval') ? undefined : syntaxErrorLine(code, msg) };
patches.why: Run Script builds a function from the script text, which the page policy refuses; say so instead of reporting a syntax error.
